note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, authored none of 9c3697d0d1). RFC 6286 Section 2.1: "The BGP Identifier is a 4-octet, unsigned, non-zero integer that should be unique within an AS. The value of the BGP Identifier for a BGP speaker is determined on startup and is the same for every local interface and every BGP peer." 9c3697d0d1 changed the Producer internal/component/bgp/reactor/config.go::parsePeerSettings only by adding the comment "// RFC 9774 Section 3" above the existing applyASSetPolicy call; the session router-id override read (peer-level overrides global) and parseRouterID's zero refusal are unchanged. Tested 'non-zero integer' stands, enforced by TestParsePeerFromTreeInvalid zero_router_id_rejected, TestRFC6286GlobalZeroRouterIDRejected and TestRFC6286NonZeroRouterIDAccepted (ran green at HEAD). Gap 'is the same for every local interface and every BGP peer' stands as the owner-approved per-peer override deviation, not counted conformant. Partial, zero whole-requirement credit. Open finding carried from 2026-10-21: the clause 'is determined on startup' departs too (reload_globals.go applyGlobalsJournaled applies a changed global router-id at runtime, owner Q3 2026-10-13); Support remaining in rfc/short/rfc6286.md now discloses it, but the {partial} annotation's Gap still names only the per-peer clause; fix: name the startup clause in the annotation's Gap so the scope record matches the disclosure. Verdict unchanged: partial.
